text:
COP rose 0.49% today to close at $145.95, capping a strong two-week rally of nearly 13%. The stock has benefited from a sharp spike in global oil prices: Brent crude topped $109 following claimed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian infrastructure and Aramco facilities on October 19th, which sent crude surging and kept energy stocks in focus. As an integrated oil producer, ConocoPhillips profits directly when crude prices rise—the current gap between world oil ($126.55/barrel) and US oil ($101.91/barrel) reflects ongoing supply concerns from Middle East escalation.

Today's modest gain came despite a slight pullback in oil prices as traders digested hopes for diplomatic progress in the region. The stock's 13% jump over two weeks shows investors rotating into energy plays ahead of what Goldman Sachs and media coverage suggest remains a volatile geopolitical backdrop affecting global energy supplies.
